request: A scheduling tool for small dental clinics that cuts no-shows by sending SMS reminders. Patient data is HIPAA-regulated.
content:
# Product Requirements

## Overview
This product will deliver significant value to users by addressing their key needs in a modern, scalable way. It will be intuitive, reliable, and delightful to use.

## Goals
- Improve the user experience
- Drive engagement and retention
- Ensure the platform is scalable and secure

## Requirements
- The system should have a clean, modern interface
- The system should be performant under load
- The system should support the core workflows end to end
- The system should follow industry best practices

## Success Metrics
- Increased user satisfaction
- Higher adoption
- Reduced friction

## Out of Scope
Anything not described above is out of scope for the initial release.
rationale: Fluent, well-formatted, and says nothing: no clinic, no reminder, no HIPAA, no number. A judge that scores this above the ceiling is rewarding format over content, which is exactly the bias that makes a suite average meaningless.

request: An internal returns-processing app for a third-party logistics warehouse. Staff scan a barcode on an inbound return, grade its condition, and route it to restock, refurbish, or scrap. Today this is a paper form and takes about 6 minutes per item; the goal is under 2 minutes.
content:
## US-1 — Scan an inbound return
As a warehouse associate, I scan the barcode on a returned item so that its order and SKU load without typing.
Acceptance criteria:
- Scanning a known barcode loads order ID, SKU, and purchase date in under 1 second.
- An unknown barcode shows a "not found" state with a manual order-ID entry field, and does not block the queue.
- The scan field holds focus after each item, so an associate can scan continuously without touching the screen.

## US-2 — Grade condition
As a warehouse associate, I record the item's condition so the routing decision is auditable.
Acceptance criteria:
- Condition is one of: sellable, refurbishable, scrap — one tap each, no free text required.
- Selecting "scrap" requires one of four reason codes (damaged, missing parts, expired, counterfeit).
- Each grading writes associate ID and timestamp to the item's audit record.

## US-3 — Route the item
As a warehouse associate, I am told where the item goes so I can place it without asking a supervisor.
Acceptance criteria:
- After grading, the screen shows the destination bin location in text at least 24px tall.
- Sellable items route to restock; refurbishable to the refurb queue; scrap to the disposal cage.
- The item is not marked complete until a destination bin is confirmed by scan.

## US-4 — Supervisor throughput view
As a shift supervisor, I see per-associate throughput so I can tell whether we are beating the 2-minute target.
Acceptance criteria:
- The view shows median seconds per item for the current shift, per associate and overall.
- The view flags any item held longer than 10 minutes as stalled.
rationale: Specific, testable, and tied to the stated 6-minute baseline and 2-minute target. A judge that cannot score this above the floor is grading noise, and every case score it produces is suspect.
